runtimeSchemaChecks.exportUniqueness: selectedFields are unique and exact targetObjectType/sourceId/sourceVersion/sourceSchemaVersion branch equality is required
runtimeSchemaChecks.digests: every digest is lowercase sha256:<64 lowercase hexadecimal characters>; exact lexical validation supplements descriptor length bounds
runtimeSchemaChecks.relations: merge relation counts contain every and only the target-specific ordered relation IDs once

workerProtocol.genesis: fatal dry-run, including header-only input, rolls back and returns the fatal public error with no job/audit/outbox/idempotency result side effect; a successful dry-run with at least one data row atomically inserts revision 1 draft plus pending rows/chunks, validates, audits, and transitions to revision 2 validated; only validated commit CAS audits and creates queued revision 3
workerProtocol.chunking: for dataRowCount in 1..10000 and zero-based parsed data-row index i, chunkIndex=floor(i/250), rowStart=250*chunkIndex, rowEndExclusive=min(rowStart+250,dataRowCount); exactly ceil(dataRowCount/250) chunks exist and include every pending input row once
rowTransitions: pending->accepted with target effect in one transaction
pending->rejected with one safe diagnostic and no target effect
workerProtocol.attempt: attempt is 1 on first claim, increments only on expiry reclaim, and is bounded at 3
workerProtocol.retryExhaustion: expiry at attempt 3 atomically marks the current and all remaining queued/claimed chunks failed, every pending row rejected with IMPORT_WORKER_RETRY_EXHAUSTED, and closes the job failed when acceptedRows=0 or partially-failed otherwise with one terminal audit/outbox; it never requeues
workerProtocol.claim: CAS locks queued or expired-claimed chunk with expected leaseRevision and persisted workerGenerationFence, then writes the current global workerGenerationFence, leaseOwnerGeneration, and leaseExpiresAt; it reauthorizes current import/target/field authority and authorization revision at claim
workerProtocol.effect: reauthorize again immediately before each row effect; pending-to-terminal row outcome and target effect are one transaction
workerProtocol.completion: reauthorize before chunk completion and final job completion; stale fence performs no state change, while revoked/stale authority atomically marks every pending row rejected with ACTION_FORBIDDEN, marks the current and all remaining chunks failed, and closes the running job failed when acceptedRows=0 or partially-failed otherwise; it never requeues
workerProtocol.revisionAudit: queued-to-running increments job revision once and writes one import-job audit and one sales.event.import-job-changed outbox; each chunk claim/reclaim increments leaseRevision only; every terminal/cancel job transition increments job revision once and writes exactly one job audit/outbox; row effects do not increment the job revision
workerProtocol.finalCounts: terminal acceptedRows=count(outcome=accepted), rejectedRows=count(outcome=rejected), processedRows=acceptedRows+rejectedRows=dataRowCount, no pending row remains, and each count equals durable import-row outcomes exactly

merge.forbidden: no loser or generic data-movement outbox

persistence.receipt: immutable application-lifetime record containing action/version, actor, authorization revision, upload/mapping/schema digests, target, counts, chunk-result digest list, artifact digests, and final state; it contains no raw sensitive cell values

import.exactOnce: each chunk is claimed only with current monotonic worker-generation fence plus expected lease revision; row insert/update effect and import-row outcome share one transaction keyed by (importJobId, oneBasedDataRow), then chunk completion/result digest commits. Crash before transaction rolls back; crash after commit retries by durable row outcome. A stale generation cannot claim or complete. Final counts derive only from durable row outcomes.
import.outcomes: row-level validation/mutation failures produce partially-failed with one diagnostic per rejected row; malformed encoding/dialect, unsafe formula, limit breach, protected field, or dry-run admission failure reject before queued work and create no target records

export.snapshot: creation materializes an authorized/redacted immutable row projection and canonical query/source/schema/authorization revisions before queueing. Worker emits only that snapshot; it never refetches broader live rows. Publish and every download recheck current export, source, record, field, and artifact authority; denial returns no bytes.
export.csvOutput: UTF-8 RFC4180 with CRLF records, comma delimiter, double-quote escaping, exactly selected authorized headers in persisted order, and no BOM. Every emitted field is first authorized/redacted and then spreadsheet-neutralized using importSchema.cellRules.whitespaceControls exactly: if removal reveals =, +, -, or @, prefix a single apostrophe; no value is otherwise transformed.

persistence.artifact: immutable bytes with digest, content type, size, createdAt, expiresAt and no inline sensitive payload in audit/receipt

worker.claim: CAS queued revision and persisted workerGenerationFence/leaseRevision, then writes the current global workerGenerationFence, leaseOwnerGeneration, leaseExpiresAt, and attempt=1; queued-to-running increments job revision and audits
worker.reclaim: expired running lease CAS-checks the persisted old workerGenerationFence, lease owner, leaseRevision, and expiry, then writes the current global fence/new owner and increments leaseRevision/attempt, at most 3 attempts; the superseded generation cannot write, publish, or complete
worker.retryExhaustion: third lease expiry CAS-transitions running-to-failed, discards staged bytes, and emits exactly one terminal audit/outbox; no requeue
worker.publish: stage bytes under exportJobId and atomically publish only after digest/count and all current source/row/field/artifact authority checks; publish CAS requires the current lease/fence/revision
worker.cancelRace: cancel CAS is accepted only while queued; claim wins by queued-to-running CAS or cancel wins by queued-to-cancelled CAS, never both; cancellation emits one audit/outbox and no bytes
worker.completion: publish plus running-to-succeeded revision increment, receipt, audit, outbox, artifact locator, digest, and row count commit once; crash replay returns the durable terminal result

candidateSource.input: the exact descriptor input fields target-object-type,id,expected-revision plus standard opaque cursor pagination capped at 100
candidateSource.output: table.records fields candidate-id,candidate-revision,match-kind plus standard opaque nextCursor; candidates are unique and ordered by candidateId ascending
candidateSource.authority: current sales.records.merge plus current subject and candidate record authority and every matching field authority; if either side's match field is not readable, omit the candidate and expose neither reason, count, overflow, nor alternate match
candidateSource.overflow: scan at most 1001 authorized unique candidates; if more than 1000 exist, return DEDUPE_CANDIDATE_LIMIT with zero rows and no count; otherwise pages contain at most 100 and hasNext is exactly whether the opaque cursor has a successor within that bounded set

normalizers.runtime: ECMAScript String.prototype.toLowerCase under exact Node 24.19.0 Unicode 17.0 ICU 78.3 after NFC; runtime/version drift requires a new normalizer version and reindex before admission
normalizers.accountNormalizedName: NFC; trim and collapse only importSchema.cellRules.whitespaceControls code points to one U+0020; then exact versioned lowercase
normalizers.contactNormalizedEmail: NFC; trim only importSchema.cellRules.whitespaceControls code points; then exact versioned lowercase; no provider-specific rewrite
normalizers.contactNormalizedPhone: NFC, retain ASCII digits only; require 7..15 digits; no country/default inference

merge.input: the exact action descriptor input; idempotency is the existing action envelope; request-local subject supplies winnerId/winnerExpectedRevision and the selected candidate supplies loserId/loserExpectedRevision
merge.winner: request-local subject is always the surviving winner and selected candidate is always the merged loser; winner retains every business value with no field coalescing, overwriting, hidden comparison, or automatic undo
merge.authority: current sales.records.merge, both locked active same-type rows in application/environment, current record authority for both, current subject/candidate matching-field authority, and expected authorization revision; stale, merged, cross-scope, self, or different-type input is denied before mutation
merge.revisions: winner business values remain byte-identical but winner revision increments exactly once for merge audit; loser revision increments exactly once and state becomes merged with protected mergedIntoId=winnerId; output winnerRevision and loserRevision are these post-commit revisions
merge.audits: two ordered immutable sales.merge.commit audits distinguish winner active->active survivor and loser active->merged outcomes through resource ID, state transition, revisions, and lineage facts; relation rewrite counts and one outbox event follow in the same transaction and are bound by lineageDigest
merge.lineage: same transaction writes immutable {lineageId,applicationId,environment,targetObjectType,winnerId,winnerPreRevision,winnerPostRevision,loserId,loserPreRevision,loserPostRevision,matchKind,normalizerVersion,actorId,authorizationRevision,winnerPreDigest,winnerPostDigest,loserPreDigest,loserPostDigest,rewrittenRelationCounts,committedAt}; pre digests cover locked rows before any write and post digests cover committed rows after revision/state/redirect changes
merge.atomicity: winner/loser locks, authority rechecks, exact rewrites, lifecycle/revision changes, lineage, audit, outbox, and idempotency result commit in one transaction or zero effects
merge.rollback: transaction rollback before commit only; post-commit automatic undo is forbidden

query.input: the exact sales.export.create@1 input schema; selectedFields are unique, belong to the source/target pair, and source version/schema/hash match exactly; filters, caller sort, offset, cursor, and page-size controls are forbidden because current source fields expose no filter/sort operators
query.ordering: materialization scans the complete authorized current source projection in stable numeric record ID ascending order using host-internal batches of at most 100

exportSchema.fences: creation locks source/schema/hash/authorization plus every selected row identity/revision, then repeats the source/schema/authorization fence immediately before queued revision 1 commit; before publish and every download recheck export/source/field/artifact and every snapshot row record revision/authority; any missing/revoked/stale row denies the whole artifact and returns no bytes
exportSchema.output: exact RFC4180 UTF-8 CRLF no-BOM artifact; rowCount<=10000 and bytes<=16777216

output.cursor: standard opaque cursor; hasNext is true exactly when another authorized row exists within the bounded candidate set

dedupeSchema.order: candidate-id ascending; one row per unique candidate
dedupeSchema.selection: subject and candidate are same application/environment/type, active, current expected revision, candidateId!=id, and both pass current record plus matching-field authority immediately before query and output
dedupeSchema.contactMatch: email equality only emits contact-email; phone equality only emits contact-phone; both equal emits contact-email-and-phone; no priority or duplicate candidate row

mergeSchema.contactAccount: lock winner and loser active Contact rows; both accountId are non-null, equal, same application/environment scope, and the locked Account remains active/current-authorized
mergeSchema.direction: request-local subject maps only to winnerId/winnerExpectedRevision and selected candidate maps only to loserId/loserExpectedRevision; both revisions are checked after locking and immediately before commit
mergeSchema.matchKind: deterministically recompute one dedupeSchema.output.matchKind under node24.19-unicode17-v1 at commit; mismatch denies
mergeSchema.output: the exact sales.merge.commit@1 outputSchema; winnerRevision and loserRevision are post-commit and each equals its locked expected revision plus one

audit.winner: sales.merge.commit with resource=winner, active->active, and winner expectedRevision->expectedRevision+1
audit.loser: sales.merge.commit with resource=loser, active->merged, loser expectedRevision->expectedRevision+1, and immutable lineageId/mergedIntoId facts
audit.lineageDigestCoverage: canonical lineage identity/scope, all pre/post revisions and row digests, exact ordered relation counts, actor, authorization revision, normalizer/match kind, committedAt

mergeSchema.mergedInto: mergedIntoId is absent on active rows, required and immutable on merged loser rows, protected from generic mutation/import, and redirect lookup reauthorizes loser and winner current record/field scope before returning winner identity

dataMovement.retention: import/export artifact bytes expire exactly 30 days after creation and are unavailable thereafter; job/row/chunk/diagnostic metadata, receipts, audit, idempotency, snapshot digest, and merge lineage remain application-lifetime

polymorphicRelatedTargets.sharedIntent: Activities, Notes, Attachment references, and optional Task links may name only this closed target vocabulary and must resolve in their own application and environment.

retention.domainRows: application-lifetime unless later accepted erasure decision
retention.mergeLineage: application-lifetime unless later accepted erasure decision
retention.audit: application-lifetime unless later accepted erasure decision

migration.legacyOpportunitySafety: account and owner use explicit receipt-bound migration identities or maintenance-required; optional contact, amount and expected close remain null; money parses losslessly or migration stops
migration.legacyTaskSafety: dueDate and relatedRecord remain optional; missing owner requires recorded configured migration owner or maintenance-required; potentialRevenue is receipt evidence only; privateNote becomes one authorized immutable Note
migration.persistedReferenceSafety: RBAC grants, template adoptions, settings, pages, publications, blocks, source/action bindings and saved views migrate atomically or fail closed
migration.pipelineStageOpaqueIdMigration: P13.4 uses fixed UUIDv5 bytes and receipt-bound mapping to atomically rewrite only mutable stage ID and allowed-transition references; immutable audit, idempotency request/result, and published-document evidence stays byte-preserved
